title: Length bound from a division invariant
statement: Let $z$ and $S$ be finite bit strings. Suppose there are finite bit strings $R,r,q$ such that $S$ is the nested self-delimiting encoding of the second decoded component of $z$, paired with the encoding of $R$ paired with the encoding of $r$ and $q$. Suppose also that $|r|+|R|≤||$ and $|q|+|R|≤||$, where $||$ denotes the length of the first decoded component of $z$ (taken to be empty if parsing fails). If the binary value of the second decoded component of $z$ is positive, then $(\operatorname{val}(q)\operatorname{val}(b)+\operatorname{val}(r))2^{|R|}+\operatorname{val}(R^{\mathrm{rev}})=\operatorname{val}(a)$ and $\operatorname{val}(r)<\operatorname{val}(b)$, where $a$ and $b$ are respectively the first and second decoded components of $z$ and $\operatorname{val}$ is the binary value of a bit string. Then $|S|≤7(|z|+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: There exist finite bit strings $R,r,q$ witnessing the nested encoding of the second decoded component of $z$
$|r|+|R|$ is at most the length of the first decoded component of $z$
$|q|+|R|$ is at most the length of the first decoded component of $z$
If the binary value of the second decoded component is positive, the stated quotient-remainder reconstruction identity holds
If the binary value of the second decoded component is positive, the binary value of $r$ is less than that of the second decoded component
caveat: The encoded nested pairing and conditional arithmetic invariant are rendered from the formal definition; the symbols $a,b$ denote the decoded components, with empty defaults on parse failure.
